name: Hiroki Ishiguro

sonic_profile.texture: gentle, clean — piano and synthesizer, oceanic and nature-themed atmosphere

philosophical_profile: Ishiguro works in the tradition of Japanese environmental music — his track 'Unity' was selected for Music From Memory's Heisei no Oto, a compilation framing the 1989-1996 CD era of Japanese music as 'kankyo ongaku adjacent.' His compositional focus on ocean and natural imagery positions music as spatial rather than performative. Less radical in approach than Yoshimura, but working in the same spirit — music as a quality you inhabit rather than a sequence you follow. A later-generation heir to the tradition, carrying it into the CD era.

sources.summary: Artist bio — piano and synthesizer focus, oceanic themes, 1992 debut.
Music From Memory selected 'Unity' for Heisei no Oto — validates kankyo ongaku adjacent placement.

notes: Primary sources are thin. No interviews available. Going off context for the philosophical framing. Recommend checking by ear before using in further connections.
